docs.title: AI Codebase Knowledge Builder
docs.text: Ever stared at a new codebase written by others feeling completely lost? This project analyzes GitHub repositories and creates beginner-friendly tutorials explaining exactly how the code works - all powered by AI! Our intelligent system automatically breaks down complex codebases into digestible explanations that even beginners can understand.

docs.title: 🚀 Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Clone this repository 

    git clone https://github.com/ardennguyen/Codebase-Knowledge-Builder

  2. Install dependencies (we highly recommend using a virtual environment of your choice like venv, conda, uv, or pyenv to avoid polluting your global system): 

    pip install -r requirements.txt

  3. Set up LLM in utils/call_llm.py by providing credentials via a .env file. You can use native Gemini by setting GEMINI_API_KEY. For OpenRouter, set LLM_PROVIDER=OPENROUTER and OPENROUTER_API_KEY.

  4. Generate a complete codebase tutorial by running the main script: 

    # Analyze a GitHub repository
python main.py --repo https://github.com/username/repo --include "*.py" "*.js" --exclude "tests/*" --max-size 50000

# Or, analyze a local directory
python main.py --dir /path/to/your/codebase --include "*.py" --exclude "*test*"

# Or, generate a tutorial in Vietnamese
python main.py --repo https://github.com/username/repo --language "Vietnamese"

docs.title: CLI Options
docs.text:
• --repo or --dir - Specify either a GitHub repo URL or a local directory path (required, mutually exclusive)
  • -n, --name - Project name (optional, derived from URL/directory if omitted)
  • -t, --token - GitHub token (or set GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable)
  • -o, --output - Output directory (default: ./output)
  • -i, --include - Files to include (e.g., *.py *.js). Defaults to * (all files).
  • -e, --exclude - Files to exclude. Custom patterns are automatically merged with a massive global exclusion list (build caches, node_modules, binaries, media, AI environments) AND your repository's native .gitignore rules.
  • -s, --max-size - Maximum file size in bytes (default: 200KB)
  • --language - Language for the generated tutorial (default: "english")
  • --max-abstractions - Maximum number of abstractions to identify (default: 10)
  • --no-cache - Disable LLM response caching (default: caching enabled)
  • --thinking-level - Thinking effort level for native Gemini, OpenRouter, and Ollama reasoning models (e.g., low, medium, high). Leave empty to use model defaults.
  • --max-tokens - Maximum number of tokens for the context window (default: fetched dynamically from the model).
  • --mode - Documentation style (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk). (default: tutorial)
  • --advanced - Legacy flag: equivalent to --mode advanced
  • --mkdocs - Format output for MkDocs Material (adds YAML frontmatter & nav snippet)
  • --incremental - Enable MD5 incremental caching to skip unchanged modules (Only supported in --mode api-reference)
  • --force-rebuild - Clear incremental cache and regenerate all chapters from scratch (use with --incremental)
  • --batch - Maximum files per batch when using map-reduce mode (default: 50).
  • --force-batch - Force the pipeline to use map-reduce mode regardless of context limits.
  • --debug - Enable verbose debug output.
  • --cleanup - Clean up logs and cache JSON at the end of the script (default: No).

The application will crawl the repository, analyze the codebase structure, generate tutorial content in the specified language, and save the output in the specified directory (default: ./output). This includes individual chapter files, an index.md, and a compiled full_content.md containing the complete tutorial with a Table of Contents.

Built using Pocket Flow, a 100-line LLM framework.

docs.title: 1. Requirements
docs.text:
Notes for AI: Keep it simple and clear. If the requirements are abstract, write concrete user stories

User Story: As a developer onboarding to a new codebase, I want a tutorial automatically generated from its GitHub repository or local directory, optionally in a specific language. The system supports four documentation styles: a tutorial mode that explains core abstractions with beginner-friendly language, analogies, and code walkthroughs; an advanced mode that produces architecture deep-dives aimed at senior developers or PMs joining a project mid-way, covering design patterns, key dependencies, and practical onboarding notes; an api-reference mode that generates exhaustive, formal API documentation for every code module (1:1 file-to-chapter mapping); and an sdk mode that produces SDK-style integration guides. The system must also gracefully handle codebases of any size by dynamically switching to a Map-Reduce approach when context limits are reached.

Input: - A publicly accessible GitHub repository URL or a local directory path. - A project name (optional, will be derived from the URL/directory if not provided). - Desired language for the tutorial (optional, defaults to English). - Advanced configurations: documentation style (--mode), token scaling (--max-tokens, --batch, --force-batch), prompting (--thinking-level, --max-abstractions), caching (--no-cache), output format (--mkdocs, --incremental), debugging (--debug), and execution cleanup (--cleanup).

Output: - A directory named after the project containing: - An index.md file with: - A high-level project summary (potentially translated). - A Mermaid flowchart diagram visualizing relationships between abstractions (using potentially translated names/labels). - An ordered list of links to chapter files (using potentially translated names). - A link to full_content.md at the bottom. - Individual Markdown files for each chapter (01_chapter_one.md, 02_chapter_two.md, etc.) detailing core abstractions in a logical order (potentially translated content). - A full_content.md (inside the project subdirectory) containing all merged chapters and a Table of Contents. - When --mkdocs is used: YAML frontmatter is injected into every chapter, filenames mirror source directory structure instead of numbered prefixes, and a nav_snippet.yml navigation file is generated for MkDocs integration. - When --incremental is used (api-reference mode only): a .doc_cache_manifest.json tracks MD5 hashes of source files to skip regeneration of unchanged modules across runs.

docs.title: 2. Flow Design
docs.text: Notes for AI: 1. Consider the design patterns of agent, map-reduce, rag, and workflow. Apply them if they fit. 2. Present a concise, high-level description of the workflow.

docs.title: Applicable Design Pattern:
docs.text:
This project primarily uses a Workflow pattern with dynamic branching into a Map-Reduce pattern. The chapter writing step also utilizes a BatchNode.

  1. Workflow & Routing: The overall process fetches code, estimates token payloads, and routes based on context limits. If the codebase fits the LLM window, it goes directly to abstraction identification.
  2. Map-Reduce: If the codebase exceeds context limits (or if forced), the codebase is grouped into token-aware, directory-isolated batches (each batch stays under the effective token limit and never mixes files from different directories). A MapAbstractions BatchNode processes each batch individually, and a ReduceAbstractions Node merges them into a global list.
  3. Batch Processing: The WriteChapters node processes each identified abstraction independently (map) before final tutorial compilation.

docs.title: Flow high-level Design:
docs.text:
1. FetchRepo: Crawls the specified repository/directory using crawl_github_files or crawl_local_files.
  2. ContextRouter: Analyzes the total token payload of the fetched files using tiktoken. Dynamically calculates prompt overhead (template tokens + directory tree tokens) and computes an effective limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead. If --mode api-reference is used, routes to "deterministic". If the file content tokens exceed this effective limit or if --force-batch is used, it chunks files into token-aware, directory-isolated batches (never mixing files from different directories) and routes to "batch". Also builds a compact directory tree of all files (stored in shared["directory_tree"]) for cross-batch awareness. With --debug, displays detailed per-batch file lists and token breakdowns. Otherwise, it routes to "direct".
  3. Path A: Direct
    • IdentifyAbstractions: Analyzes the entire codebase at once to identify core abstractions.
  4. Path B: Map-Reduce
    • MapAbstractions (BatchNode): Analyzes each localized directory chunk to extract partial abstractions. Each batch receives the full directory tree for cross-batch awareness.
    • ReduceAbstractions: Merges overlapping/partial abstractions into a global list of architecture components.
  5. Path C: Deterministic (api-reference mode)
    • DeterministicFileMapper: Bypasses LLM-based abstraction discovery entirely. Uses a lightweight LLM call to filter out non-code files (configs, UI layouts, static assets), then creates a 1:1 mapping of each code file to a documentation module. Skips AnalyzeRelationships and OrderChapters, routing directly to WriteChapters.
  6. AnalyzeRelationships (Paths A & B only): Takes the unified abstractions list (from either path) and generates a high-level project summary and relationships diagram. Uses token-budget-aware file inclusion: the budget is split evenly across abstractions, with unused budget redistributed in a second pass, maximizing code context without exceeding the context window.
  7. OrderChapters (Paths A & B only): Determines the most logical sequence to present the abstractions.
  8. WriteChapters (BatchNode): Iterates through the ordered abstractions and writes detailed Markdown chapters using context-aware code inclusion.
  9. CombineTutorial: Assembles the final outputs including index.md, individual chapter files, and a compiled full_content.md.
flowchart TD
    A[FetchRepo] --> Router[ContextRouter]

    Router -->|direct| B[IdentifyAbstractions]
    Router -->|batch| M1[MapAbstractions]
    Router -->|deterministic| DFM[DeterministicFileMapper]
    M1 --> M2[ReduceAbstractions]

    B --> C[AnalyzeRelationships]
    M2 --> C

    C --> D[OrderChapters]
    D --> E[Batch WriteChapters]
    DFM --> E
    E --> F[CombineTutorial]

def crawl_local_files(directory, include_patterns=None, exclude_patterns=None,
                      max_file_size=None, use_relative_paths=True) -> dict:
    # Returns: {"files": {relative_path_str: content_str, ...}}

Directory Pruning Algorithm (critical for nested directories like Core.User/.vs/): 

# During os.walk, for each subdirectory d:
excluded_dirs = set()
for d in dirs:
    dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), directory)
    # Check .gitignore first
    if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
        excluded_dirs.add(d)
        continue
    # Check exclude patterns — strip trailing /* for directory matching
    if exclude_patterns:
        for pattern in exclude_patterns:
            dir_pattern = pattern[:-2] if pattern.endswith("/*") else pattern
            if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                break
# Remove matched dirs to prevent os.walk descent
for d in dirs.copy():
    if d in excluded_dirs:
        dirs.remove(d)

Note: Directory validation: raises ValueError if directory path doesn't exist. Loads .gitignore with utf-8-sig encoding (BOM-safe). All directories and files are sorted() for deterministic traversal order.

Progress Display Format: - Green (\033[92m): [processed] — Successfully read files - Gray (\033[90m): [excluded (.gitignore)] / [excluded (not in include list)] — Skipped by pattern - Red (\033[91m): [size limit: {size_kb:.0f}KB] — Exceeded max_file_size - Red (\033[91m): [cannot process: not a text file] / [cannot process: {e}] — Binary/encoding errors

Note: After crawling, prints a --- Crawl Summary --- block with total found, processed, excluded, size limited, and non-text counts.

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdirname:
    print(f"Cloning SSH repo {repo_url} to temp dir {tmpdirname} ...")
    try:
        repo = git.Repo.clone_from(repo_url, tmpdirname)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error cloning repo: {e}")
        return {"files": {}, "stats": {"error": str(e)}}

    files = {}
    skipped_files = []

    # --- ANSI colors ---
    C_GREEN  = "\033[92m"
    C_GRAY   = "\033[90m"
    C_RED    = "\033[91m"
    C_RESET  = "\033[0m"

    # --- Counters ---
    count_processed = 0
    count_excluded = 0
    count_size_limit = 0
    count_non_text = 0
    skipped_size_list = []
    skipped_non_text_list = []
    entry_num = 0

    # --- Load .gitignore (BOM-safe) ---
    gitignore_path = os.path.join(tmpdirname, ".gitignore")
    gitignore_spec = None
    if os.path.exists(gitignore_path):
        try:
            with open(gitignore_path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", f.readlines())
        except Exception:
            pass

    for root, dirs, filenames in os.walk(tmpdirname):
        # --- Directory pruning (same algorithm as crawl_local_files) ---
        excluded_dirs = set()
        for d in sorted(dirs):
            dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), tmpdirname)
            reason = None
            if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
                reason = "excluded (.gitignore)"
            elif exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    dir_pattern = pattern[:-2] if pattern.endswith("/*") else pattern
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                        reason = "excluded"
                        break
            if reason:
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                entry_num += 1
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {dirpath_rel}/ [{reason}]{C_RESET}")

        for d in dirs.copy():
            if d in excluded_dirs:
                dirs.remove(d)
        dirs.sort()  # Deterministic traversal order

        # --- File processing ---
        for filename in sorted(filenames):
            abs_path = os.path.join(root, filename)
            rel_path = os.path.relpath(abs_path, tmpdirname)
            entry_num += 1

            if not should_include_file(rel_path, filename, gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [excluded]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            try:
                file_size = os.path.getsize(abs_path)
            except OSError:
                continue

            if file_size > max_file_size:
                count_size_limit += 1
                skipped_size_list.append(rel_path)
                size_kb = file_size / 1024
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [size limit: {size_kb:.0f}KB]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            try:
                with open(abs_path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                files[rel_path] = content
                count_processed += 1
                print(f"{C_GREEN}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [processed]{C_RESET}")
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [cannot process: not a text file]{C_RESET}")
            except Exception as e:
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [cannot process: {e}]{C_RESET}")

    # --- Crawl Summary ---
    total_fetched = count_processed + count_excluded + count_size_limit + count_non_text
    print(f"\n--- Crawl Summary ---")
    print(f"  Total found : {total_fetched}")
    print(f"{C_GREEN}  Processed   : {count_processed}{C_RESET}")
    if count_excluded > 0:
        print(f"{C_GRAY}  Excluded    : {count_excluded}{C_RESET}")
    if count_size_limit > 0:
        print(f"{C_RED}  Size limit  : {count_size_limit}{C_RESET}")
        for sf in skipped_size_list:
            print(f"{C_RED}    - {sf}{C_RESET}")
    if count_non_text > 0:
        print(f"{C_RED}  Non-text    : {count_non_text}{C_RESET}")
        for sf in skipped_non_text_list:
            print(f"{C_RED}    - {sf}{C_RESET}")
    print(f"---------------------")

    return {
        "files": files,
        "stats": {
            "downloaded_count": len(files),
            "skipped_count": len(skipped_files),
            "skipped_files": skipped_files,
            "base_path": None,
            "include_patterns": include_patterns,
            "exclude_patterns": exclude_patterns,
            "source": "ssh_clone"
        }
    }

Step 2 — Dynamic Branch Detection (handles multi-segment branch names like feature/foo): 

if len(path_parts) > 2 and 'tree' == path_parts[2]:

else:

Step 4 — Recursive Content Fetching (1 API call per directory): 

def fetch_contents(path):
    url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}"
    params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}
    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=(30, 30))

    # Rate limit handling with header-based wait:
    if response.status_code in (403, 429) and 'rate limit exceeded' in response.text.lower():
        if not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Provide a token.")
        reset_time = int(response.headers.get('X-RateLimit-Reset', 0))
        wait_time = max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1
        time.sleep(wait_time)
        return fetch_contents(path)  # Recursive retry

    contents = response.json()
    if not isinstance(contents, list):
        contents = [contents]

    for item in contents:
        if item["type"] == "file":
            # Check patterns, size, then fetch content
            # Path A: Use download_url directly, check Content-Length header
            # Path B (fallback): If no download_url, GET item["url"],
            #   base64 decode with size estimate: len(content) * 0.75 > max_file_size
        elif item["type"] == "dir":
            # Check gitignore + exclude before recursing
            fetch_contents(item["path"])

Step 5 — Dual Content Fetch Strategy: 

# Path A: download_url available
if "download_url" in item and item["download_url"]:
    file_response = requests.get(item["download_url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
    content_length = int(file_response.headers.get('content-length', 0))
    if content_length > max_file_size:  # Final size check
        continue
    files[rel_path] = file_response.text

# Path B: base64 fallback
else:
    content_response = requests.get(item["url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
    content_data = content_response.json()
    if len(content_data["content"]) * 0.75 > max_file_size:  # Approximate size
        continue
    file_content = base64.b64decode(content_data["content"]).decode('utf-8')
    files[rel_path] = file_content

No LLM call. Routes to "direct" or "batch". Writes shared["max_tokens"], shared["file_batches"], shared["directory_tree"].

ContextRouter Algorithm: 1. Auto-detect max_tokens from provider if not set; write to shared["max_tokens"] 2. Measure prompt overhead = max(template_tokens for tutorial/advanced map_abstractions.md) + directory_tree_tokens 3. safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95); effective_limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead 4. Count total file content tokens using f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n" per file 5. If total_tokens > effective_limit OR force_batch: - Group files by os.path.dirname(path) — NEVER mix directories - Within each directory group, create batches respecting both effective_limit tokens AND batch_size file count - Return "batch" 6. Else: Return "direct"

other_dir/

def create_token_counter():

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The flow.py module defines the workflow orchestration layer of the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. It constructs a declarative directed acyclic graph (DAG) using the pocketflow framework to automate the end-to-end extraction, analysis, structuring, and synthesis of codebase documentation and tutorials.

The module provides a single factory function, create_tutorial_flow(), which initializes pipeline execution nodes defined in nodes and wires them together with deterministic and conditional branching edges. The pipeline dynamically routes execution based on repository token limits and processing strategies, handling three distinct architectural workflows:

  1. Direct Path: For smaller codebases that fit within standard context windows, routing directly to single-pass abstraction identification.
  2. Batch (Map-Reduce) Path: For large repositories that exceed token limits, breaking files into chunks, mapping abstractions in parallel/batches, and reducing them into a unified concept list.
  3. Deterministic Path: For structured 1:1 file-to-chapter generation, bypassing dynamic concept discovery to build dedicated documentation chapters per source file.

docs.title: create_tutorial_flow()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def create_tutorial_flow() -> Flow

Description: Instantiates and interconnects all execution nodes required to process a codebase into a cohesive multi-chapter tutorial. Nodes interacting with external Large Language Model (LLM) APIs are configured with exponential backoff and retry parameters (max_retries=5, wait=20) to ensure network resilience and handle API rate limits.

The pipeline defines directional connections using pocketflow's overloaded shift (>>) and minus (-) operators: * >> establishes an unconditional sequential transition between two nodes. * - "action" >> establishes a conditional transition triggered when the upstream node returns a specific routing action string ("direct", "batch", or "deterministic").

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * Flow: An initialized pocketflow.Flow instance configured with FetchRepo as its root entry node (start=fetch_repo).

Raises: * Does not raise exceptions during graph construction. Runtime exceptions during flow execution are managed by individual node retry policies and PocketFlow's execution runner.

Example: 

def create_tutorial_flow():
    fetch_repo = FetchRepo()
    context_router = ContextRouter()
    map_abstractions = MapAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    reduce_abstractions = ReduceAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    identify_abstractions = IdentifyAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    analyze_relationships = AnalyzeRelationships(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    order_chapters = OrderChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    write_chapters = WriteChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    combine_tutorial = CombineTutorial()
    deterministic_mapper = DeterministicFileMapper(max_retries=5, wait=20)

    fetch_repo >> context_router

    context_router - "direct" >> identify_abstractions
    context_router - "batch" >> map_abstractions
    context_router - "deterministic" >> deterministic_mapper

    map_abstractions >> reduce_abstractions

    identify_abstractions >> analyze_relationships
    reduce_abstractions >> analyze_relationships

    analyze_relationships >> order_chapters
    order_chapters >> write_chapters

    deterministic_mapper >> write_chapters

    write_chapters >> combine_tutorial

    return Flow(start=fetch_repo)

The function begins by instantiating the ingestion nodes: FetchRepo, which retrieves the target repository files (from either local storage or GitHub), and ContextRouter, which calculates total token volume to determine the processing strategy. It configures LLM-dependent nodes (MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions, IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters, WriteChapters, DeterministicFileMapper) with a 5-retry limit and a 20-second wait interval between retries.

Next, it defines the routing branches using PocketFlow's syntax. ContextRouter evaluates the token context size and emits an action: * If "direct" is emitted, control transitions to IdentifyAbstractions, extracting high-level system components in a single prompt. * If "batch" is emitted, control transitions to MapAbstractions, which analyzes file subsets independently before forwarding results to ReduceAbstractions to synthesize overlapping abstractions. * If "deterministic" is emitted, control routes to DeterministicFileMapper to generate fixed chapter definitions mapping 1:1 with files in the codebase.

Following abstraction resolution, both the direct and batch branches converge at AnalyzeRelationships to generate cross-component dependency diagrams, followed by OrderChapters to sequence chapters pedagogically. Both the ordered dynamic chapters and deterministic file chapters flow into WriteChapters to draft full Markdown tutorials. Finally, WriteChapters streams its outputs into CombineTutorial, which assembles the complete index, navigations, and output documents.

docs.text:
# Resolve mode (backward compatibility for --advanced)
    doc_mode = "advanced" if args.advanced else args.mode

    # Enforce incremental cache constraints
    if args.incremental and doc_mode != "api-reference":
        print(
            "\n\033[93m[Warning] --incremental caching is only effective in 'api-reference' mode due to stable 1:1 file mapping. Disabling incremental cache for this run.\033[0m\n"
        )
        args.incremental = False

    # Handle --force-rebuild: delete the cache manifest to force fresh generation
    if args.force_rebuild and args.incremental:
        project_name = args.name
        if not project_name:
            # Derive project name the same way FetchRepo does
            if args.dir:
                project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(args.dir))
            elif args.repo:
                project_name = args.repo.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]
        if project_name:
            output_base = args.output or "output"
            manifest_path = os.path.join(output_base, project_name, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
            if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
                os.remove(manifest_path)
                print(f"\033[93m[Force Rebuild] Deleted cache manifest: {manifest_path}\033[0m")
            else:
                print(f"\033[93m[Force Rebuild] No cache manifest found at {manifest_path} — all chapters will be generated fresh.\033[0m")
    elif args.force_rebuild and not args.incremental:
        print("\033[93m[Warning] --force-rebuild has no effect without --incremental. Ignoring.\033[0m")

The incremental caching subsystem relies on deterministic 1:1 file-to-chapter mappings. When --incremental is requested outside of api-reference mode, main() disables the flag and issues a console warning. When --force-rebuild is active alongside --incremental, main() derives the project name from the target path or URL, locates .doc_cache_manifest.json inside the output directory, and deletes it before flow execution starts.

docs.title: get_content_for_indices()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_content_for_indices(files_data, indices) -> dict:

Description: Extracts file content for a sequence of numeric file indices and maps them into a dictionary keyed by formatted index-and-path strings. This keyed representation provides clear file identification context within prompt structures.

Parameters: * files_data (list): List of (path, content) tuples representing all crawled files. * indices (list): Collection of integer indices pointing to specific entries in files_data.

Returns: * dict: Mapping where keys are formatted as "{i} # {path}" and values are the corresponding string contents.

Raises: * None. Out-of-bounds indices are ignored via internal bounds check 0 <= i < len(files_data).

Example: 

def get_content_for_indices(files_data, indices):
    content_map = {}
    for i in indices:
        if 0 <= i < len(files_data):
            path, content = files_data[i]
            content_map[f"{i} # {path}"] = content  # Use index + path as key for context
    return content_map

The function iterates over the requested list of indices and performs bounds checking against the files_data sequence. For each valid index, it constructs a descriptive key combining the numeric index and the original file path. Invalid or out-of-range indices are silently omitted, ensuring prompts do not receive dangling references or trigger index errors during processing.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None) -> str:

Description: Resolves and loads prompt template markdown files from the filesystem relative to the prompts/ subdirectories (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, etc.).

Parameters: * template_name (str): Base filename of the prompt markdown template (without .md). * advanced_mode (bool): Fallback flag used if mode is None. Selects between "advanced" and "tutorial". Defaults to False. * mode (str, optional): Specific mode folder override (e.g., "tutorial", "advanced", "api-reference"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: Raw text content of the loaded markdown prompt template.

Raises: * FileNotFoundError: If the constructed template path does not exist on disk. * OSError: If the file cannot be opened or read.

Example: 

def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None):
    """Load a prompt template file from the prompts/ directory."""
    if mode is None:
        prompt_dir = "advanced" if advanced_mode else "tutorial"
    else:
        prompt_dir = mode

    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "prompts", prompt_dir, f"{template_name}.md")
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        return f.read()

This helper handles path resolution across different execution contexts by referencing the absolute directory of nodes.py. It prioritizes the explicit mode parameter, falling back to the legacy advanced_mode boolean toggle if mode is not supplied. The file is opened with utf-8-sig encoding to automatically handle byte order marks present in cross-platform template assets.

docs.title: parse_yaml_response()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_yaml_response(response: str) -> Any:

Description: Parses LLM markdown outputs containing code blocks delimited by ```yaml and deserializes the enclosed payload into Python data structures.

Parameters: * response (str): Raw text output returned from an LLM call.

Returns: * Any: Deserialized YAML content (typically a dict or list).

Raises: * ValueError: Raised when the output cannot be split on ```yaml or if yaml.safe_load fails to parse the string.

Example: 

def parse_yaml_response(response):
    """Extract and parse YAML from an LLM response fenced in ```yaml blocks."""
    try:
        yaml_str = response.strip().split("```yaml")[1].split("```")[0].strip()
        return yaml.safe_load(yaml_str)
    except Exception as e:
        raise ValueError(f"Failed to parse YAML: {e}") from e

The function extracts structured data from LLM responses by finding the first ```yaml delimiter and reading up to the subsequent closing ``` code fence. It strips extraneous leading or trailing whitespace before passing the block to yaml.safe_load. Any failure during slicing or YAML parsing is wrapped and raised as a ValueError with contextual diagnostics.

docs.title: create_token_counter()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def create_token_counter() -> Callable[[str], int]:

Description: Factory function that creates a token counting callable using tiktoken with the cl100k_base encoding, falling back to a character heuristic if tiktoken fails.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * Callable[[str], int]: A function that accepts a string and returns an integer representing the token count.

Raises: * None. Handles missing dependencies or encoding errors internally by providing a fallback lambda.

Example: 

def create_token_counter():
    """Create a token counting function using tiktoken with char-count fallback."""
    try:
        enc = tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
        return lambda text: len(enc.encode(text, disallowed_special=()))
    except Exception:
        return lambda text: len(text) // 4

This factory provides a unified token counting interface across all pipeline nodes. It attempts to load the cl100k_base byte-pair encoding from tiktoken, disabling special token checks to prevent syntax errors on raw code strings. If tiktoken initialization fails, it returns a 4-characters-per-token heuristic function (len(text) // 4).

docs.title: resolve_max_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve_max_tokens(shared: dict) -> int:

Description: Determines the maximum context length for LLM interactions. It checks the shared pipeline dictionary first and falls back to inspecting active environment variables and querying model metadata.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared state dictionary passed across pipeline nodes.

Returns: * int: Maximum context window length in tokens.

Raises: * None. Defaults to standard provider context limits via get_model_context_length().

Example: 

def resolve_max_tokens(shared):
    """Resolve max_tokens from shared store or auto-detect from provider env vars."""
    max_tokens = shared.get("max_tokens")
    if max_tokens is not None:
        return max_tokens
    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if provider == "GEMINI" or not provider:
        endpoint = "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com"
        model_name = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")
        api_key = os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY", "")
    else:
        endpoint = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_BASE_URL", "")
        model_name = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", "")
        api_key = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_API_KEY", "")
    return get_model_context_length(endpoint, model_name, api_key)

The resolution checks for an explicit max_tokens configuration in the shared dictionary. If not found, it inspects LLM_PROVIDER environment variables to determine the provider endpoint, target model name, and API key. It passes these values to get_model_context_length() from utils.call_llm to dynamically look up the model's token limit.

Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Prepares the filtering prompt by listing all crawled files and combining them with project metadata for LLM evaluation.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared pipeline state containing files and project_name.

Returns: * tuple: (prompt: str, thinking_level: Optional[int], max_tokens: int).

Example: 

    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]

        file_listing = "\n".join([f"{i} # {path}" for i, (path, _) in enumerate(files_data)])

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> list[int]:

Description: Dispatches the filtering prompt to the LLM, logs token metrics, and parses the returned YAML list of valid source code indices.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Unpacked tuple from prep() containing (prompt, thinking_level, max_tokens).

Returns: * list[int]: Parsed list of validated file index integers.

Raises: * Exception: Logs and re-raises any error occurring during LLM execution or parsing.

Example: 

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        try:
            prompt, thinking_level, max_tokens = prep_res
            log_token_estimation(self.__class__.__name__, prompt, max_tokens)
            print("Smartly filtering non-code files using LLM...")
            response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=True, thinking_level=thinking_level)
            valid_indices = parse_yaml_response(response)
            if not isinstance(valid_indices, list):
                valid_indices = []
            return [int(idx) for idx in valid_indices]
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"\033[93m[Node {self.__class__.__name__} Retry Triggered] Error: {e}\033[0m")
            llm_logger.error(f"[Node {self.__class__.__name__}] Error: {e}", exc_info=True)
            raise e

exec logs estimated token usage using utils.token_utils before calling utils.call_llm with response caching enabled. The returned YAML payload is extracted and coerced into integer file indices, skipping non-code assets like assets, configuration files, or logs.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: tuple, exec_res: list[int]) -> str:

Description: Constructs deterministic module records for all retained code files, populates chapter order and placeholder relationships in shared state, and routes to "default".

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared pipeline state dictionary. * prep_res (tuple): Output from prep(). * exec_res (list[int]): List of integer indices from exec().

Returns: * str: Action "default" to transition to the next pipeline node.

Example: 

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
        import os

        files = shared.get("files", [])
        valid_indices = set(exec_res)
        modules = []
        chapter_order = []

        for idx, (file_path, content) in enumerate(files):
            if idx not in valid_indices:
                print(f"  - Skipping non-code file: {file_path}")
                continue

            clean_name = os.path.splitext(file_path)[0].replace(os.sep, ".").replace("/", ".")

            modules.append(
                {"name": clean_name, "description": f"Internal API reference for `{file_path}`", "files": [idx], "original_path": file_path}
            )
            chapter_order.append(len(modules) - 1)

        shared["abstractions"] = modules
        shared["chapter_order"] = chapter_order
        shared["relationships"] = {"summary": "Deterministic Internal API Reference.", "details": []}
        print(f"\033[92m[DeterministicFileMapper] Mapped {len(modules)} ACTUAL code files for exhaustive documentation.\033[0m")
        return "default"

The method iterates over all candidate files, skipping indices not present in valid_indices. For each retained file, it normalizes the path into a dotted module name, sets up an abstraction entry referencing the single file, builds sequential chapter ordering, and initializes static relationship metadata.

docs.title: ContextRouter
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Inherits from: pocketflow.Node

Calculates prompt and file token overhead, partitions large repositories into token-bounded batches grouped by directory structure, and selects the processing route ("direct", "batch", or "deterministic").

docs.title: ContextRouter.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Computes token usage across prompt templates, directory trees, and source files, compares total volume against context limits, and decides the routing strategy.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared pipeline state containing files, max_tokens, mode, and optional flags.

Returns: * tuple: Route metadata containing (route_type, files_data, effective_limit, batch_size, file_token_map, count_tokens, directory_tree, debug).

Example: 

    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)
        shared["max_tokens"] = max_tokens
        count_tokens = create_token_counter()
        // ... Template token overhead and directory tree calculation ...
        total_tokens = 0
        file_token_map = []
        for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
            entry = f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"
            tokens = count_tokens(entry)
            total_tokens += tokens
            file_token_map.append(tokens)

        safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)
        effective_limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead
        force_batch = shared.get("force_batch", False)

        if shared.get("mode", "tutorial") == "api-reference":
            return ("deterministic", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50), None, None, directory_tree, False)
        if total_tokens > effective_limit or force_batch:
            return ("batch", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50), file_token_map, count_tokens, directory_tree, shared.get("debug", False))
        return ("direct", files_data, effective_limit, shared.get("batch_size", 50), None, None, directory_tree, False)

prep measures prompt overhead (the larger of tutorial or advanced template sizes plus the directory tree token weight). It computes exact token counts for each individual file entry and applies a 95% safety margin on max_tokens. If the repository fits within the effective limit and force_batch is false, it routes to "direct"; otherwise, it routes to "batch" or "deterministic".

docs.title: ContextRouter.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> Union[str, list]:

Description: If batching is required, groups files by directory and splits them into token-bounded batches that do not mix directories.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Tuple from prep() containing routing and token information.

Returns: * Union[str, list]: The string "direct" or "deterministic", or a list of batches where each batch is a list of (index, path, content) tuples.

Example: 

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        route, files_data, effective_limit, batch_size, file_token_map, _count_tokens, directory_tree, debug = prep_res
        if route in ("direct", "deterministic"):
            return route

        dir_groups = defaultdict(list)
        for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
            dir_groups[os.path.dirname(path)].append((i, path, content, file_token_map[i]))

        batches = []
        for dirname in sorted(dir_groups.keys()):
            current_batch = []
            current_tokens = 0
            for i, path, content, tokens in dir_groups[dirname]:
                if current_batch and (current_tokens + tokens > effective_limit or len(current_batch) >= batch_size):
                    batches.append(current_batch)
                    current_batch = []
                    current_tokens = 0
                current_batch.append((i, path, content))
                current_tokens += tokens
            if current_batch:
                batches.append(current_batch)

        self._directory_tree = directory_tree
        return batches

When batching, files are grouped by their parent directory path. The method iterates through each directory group in sorted order, accumulating files into a batch until adding another file would exceed either effective_limit tokens or batch_size files. Batches never mix files from different directories, maintaining structural coherence.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: tuple, exec_res: Union[str, list]) -> str:

Description: Persists calculated batches and the global directory tree string into shared, returning the active route name.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared pipeline state dictionary. * prep_res (tuple): Output tuple from prep(). * exec_res (Union[str, list]): String route name or list of generated batches from exec().

Returns: * str: Route action ("direct", "deterministic", or "batch").

Example: 

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res):
        if exec_res == "direct":
            return "direct"
        if exec_res == "deterministic":
            return "deterministic"
        shared["file_batches"] = exec_res
        # Reuse directory tree built during prep()
        shared["directory_tree"] = getattr(self, "_directory_tree", self._build_directory_tree(shared["files"]))
        return "batch"

The method passes "direct" or "deterministic" straight through to trigger corresponding branch transitions in the flow. For "batch" execution, it populates shared["file_batches"] with the partitioned file lists and caches the pre-built directory_tree string in shared.

docs.title: ContextRouter._build_directory_tree()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _build_directory_tree(files_data: list) -> str:

Description: Generates an indented, compact text representation of the directory hierarchy annotated with file indices.

Parameters: * files_data (list): List of (path, content) tuples representing all files.

Returns: * str: Formatted multi-line string representing the directory tree.

Example: 

    @staticmethod
    def _build_directory_tree(files_data):
        """Build a compact directory tree string from the list of (path, content) tuples."""
        from collections import defaultdict

        dir_files = defaultdict(list)
        for i, (path, _content) in enumerate(files_data):
            dirname = os.path.dirname(path) or "."
            basename = os.path.basename(path)
            dir_files[dirname].append(f"{basename} (idx:{i})")

        lines = []
        for dirname in sorted(dir_files.keys()):
            lines.append(f"{dirname}/")
            for fname in sorted(dir_files[dirname]):
                lines.append(f"  {fname}")
        return "\n".join(lines)

This static helper builds a directory map from file paths. It groups basenames under sorted directory keys and formats them with two-space indentation, appending (idx:N) next to each file.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, item: dict) -> list[dict]:

Description: Formats prompt context for a single batch, calls the LLM to extract partial abstractions, and validates file index boundaries.

Parameters: * item (dict): Batch configuration dictionary prepared by prep().

Returns: * list[dict]: List of validated abstraction dictionaries with name, description, and sorted unique files indices.

Example: 

    def exec(self, item):
        batch_index = item["batch_index"]
        files = item["files"]
        // ... build context and format prompt template ...
        response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(item["use_cache"] and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=item["thinking_level"])
        abstractions = parse_yaml_response(response)

        validated_abstractions = []
        if isinstance(abstractions, list):
            for obj in abstractions:
                if isinstance(obj, dict) and "name" in obj and "description" in obj and "file_indices" in obj:
                    import re
                    validated_indices = []
                    for idx_entry in obj["file_indices"]:
                        nums = re.findall(r"\d+", str(idx_entry))
                        if nums:
                            validated_indices.append(int(nums[0]))
                    if validated_indices:
                        validated_abstractions.append(
                            {"name": obj["name"], "description": obj["description"], "files": sorted(list(set(validated_indices)))}
                        )
        return validated_abstractions

exec formats the batch's files into prompt context and loads the map_abstractions template. After receiving the LLM response, it parses the YAML payload and validates each abstraction object. Regular expressions extract integer file indices, deduplicating and sorting them into the final files field.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Inherits from: pocketflow.Node

Extracts core concepts and architectural abstractions directly in a single pass when the repository fits within the active context window.

docs.title: IdentifyAbstractions.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Concatenates file contents within a 95% safety token budget and prepares abstraction discovery prompt parameters.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared pipeline state containing files, project_name, and settings.

Returns: * tuple: Parameters for abstraction discovery.

Example: 

    def prep(self, shared):
        files_data = shared["files"]
        project_name = shared["project_name"]
        language = shared.get("language", "english")
        use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)
        max_abstraction_num = shared.get("max_abstraction_num", 10)
        thinking_level = shared.get("thinking_level", None)

        def create_llm_context(files_data):
            max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)
            safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)
            count_tokens = create_token_counter()
            context = ""
            file_info = []
            current_tokens = 0
            for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
                entry = f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"
                entry_tokens = count_tokens(entry)
                if current_tokens + entry_tokens > safety_limit:
                    print(f"\033[93mWarning: Context truncated at file index {i} ({path}) to fit within limit of {safety_limit} tokens.\033[0m")
                    break
                context += entry
                file_info.append((i, path))
                current_tokens += entry_tokens
            return context, file_info

        context, file_info = create_llm_context(files_data)
        file_listing_for_prompt = "\n".join([f"- {idx} # {path}" for idx, path in file_info])
        return (context, file_listing_for_prompt, len(files_data), project_name, language, use_cache, max_abstraction_num, thinking_level, shared.get("advanced_mode", False), shared.get("max_tokens", 100000), shared.get("mode", "tutorial"))

The nested create_llm_context function tracks token accumulation against a 95% safety threshold. If the budget is reached, context is truncated with a warning. It returns the combined context string alongside an indexed file listing for the prompt.

docs.title: IdentifyAbstractions.exec()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> list[dict]:

Description: Calls the LLM to identify high-level abstractions, parsing the YAML response and resolving file indices (including hyphenated range syntax like 0-3).

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Parameters from prep().

Returns: * list[dict]: List of validated abstractions with name, description, and files index lists.

Raises: * Exception: Logs and re-raises any error occurring during LLM execution or validation.

Example: 

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        try:
            (context, file_listing_for_prompt, total_files_count, project_name, language, use_cache, max_abstraction_num, thinking_level, _advanced_mode, max_tokens, doc_mode) = prep_res
            // ... load prompt template and inject language hints ...
            response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)
            abstractions = parse_yaml_response(response)
            if not isinstance(abstractions, list):
                raise ValueError("LLM Output is not a list")

            validated_abstractions = []
            for item in abstractions:
                // ... validate keys ...
                validated_indices = []
                for idx_entry in item["file_indices"]:
                    idx_str = str(idx_entry).split("#")[0].strip()
                    if "-" in idx_str:
                        parts = idx_str.split("-")
                        if len(parts) == 2:
                            start_idx = int(re.findall(r"\d+", parts[0])[0])
                            end_idx = int(re.findall(r"\d+", parts[1])[0])
                            for idx in range(start_idx, end_idx + 1):
                                if 0 <= idx < total_files_count:
                                    validated_indices.append(idx)
                            continue
                    nums = re.findall(r"\d+", idx_str)
                    if nums and 0 <= int(nums[0]) < total_files_count:
                        validated_indices.append(int(nums[0]))

                item["files"] = sorted(list(set(validated_indices)))
                validated_abstractions.append({"name": item["name"], "description": item["description"], "files": item["files"]})
            return validated_abstractions
        except Exception as e:

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Inherits from: pocketflow.Node

Extracts architectural relationships, dependencies, and data flows between discovered abstractions using a two-pass token redistribution algorithm.

flowchart TD
    Init[Calculate Total Token Budget] --> Pass1[Pass 1: Allocate Equal Budget per Abstraction]
    Pass1 --> Check[Check for Unused Budget]
    Check -->|Unused tokens remain| Pass2[Pass 2: Redistribute to Deficit Abstractions]
    Check -->|No unused tokens| Context[Construct Context with File Snippets]
    Pass2 --> Context
    Context --> Exec[AnalyzeRelationships.exec - LLM Analysis]

docs.title: AnalyzeRelationships.prep()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple:

Description: Constructs relationship context using a two-pass token redistribution algorithm that budgets file snippets evenly across abstractions and reallocates leftover capacity.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared pipeline state containing abstractions, files, and token settings.

Returns: * tuple: Context string, abstraction listings, and execution parameters.

Example: 

    def prep(self, shared):
        // ... build initial abstraction listing ...
        max_tokens = shared.get("max_tokens", 100000)
        safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)
        prompt_overhead = 2000
        total_budget = safety_limit - estimate_tokens(context) - prompt_overhead
        num_abstractions = len(abstractions)

        per_abstr_budget = total_budget // max(num_abstractions, 1)
        included_indices = set()
        abstr_results = []

        # Pass 1: Allocate equal share
        for i, sized in enumerate(abstr_file_data):
            budget = per_abstr_budget
            included_files, remaining_files = [], []
            for idx, path, file_content, tokens in sized:
                if idx in included_indices:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                    continue
                if tokens <= budget:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                    budget -= tokens
                    included_indices.add(idx)
                else:
                    remaining_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
            abstr_results.append((included_files, remaining_files, budget))

        # Pass 2: Redistribute unused budget
        total_unused = sum(r[2] for r in abstr_results)
        if total_unused > 0:
            for i, (included_files, remaining_files, _unused) in enumerate(abstr_results):
                if not remaining_files or total_unused <= 0:
                    continue
                still_remaining = []
                for idx, path, file_content, tokens in remaining_files:
                    if idx in included_indices:
                        included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                        continue
                    if tokens <= total_unused:
                        included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                        total_unused -= tokens
                        included_indices.add(idx)
                    else:
                        still_remaining.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                abstr_results[i] = (included_files, still_remaining, 0)
        // ... build context string from abstr_results ...
        return (context, "\n".join(abstraction_info_for_prompt), num_abstractions, project_name, language, use_cache, thinking_level, shared.get("advanced_mode", False), shared.get("max_tokens", 100000), shared.get("mode", "tutorial"))

To prevent early abstractions from starving later ones, prep splits available context tokens evenly across all abstractions in Pass 1, prioritizing the largest files within each abstraction. In Pass 2, unused token budget from smaller abstractions is redistributed to abstractions with remaining unallocated files. Duplicate files across abstractions are referenced by name rather than re-injected.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> list[int]:

Description: Prompts the LLM for chapter sequencing and verifies that the output forms a valid permutation containing every abstraction index exactly once.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Unpacked parameter tuple from prep().

Returns: * list[int]: Ordered permutation of abstraction indices.

Raises: * ValueError: If indices are out of bounds, duplicated, non-numeric, or if any abstraction is omitted.

Example: 

    def exec(self, prep_res):
        try:
            (abstraction_listing, context, num_abstractions, project_name, list_lang_note, use_cache, thinking_level, _advanced_mode, max_tokens, doc_mode) = prep_res
            prompt_template = load_prompt_template("order_chapters", mode=doc_mode)
            prompt = prompt_template.format(project_name=project_name, list_lang_note=list_lang_note, abstraction_listing=abstraction_listing, context=context)
            response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)

            ordered_indices_raw = parse_yaml_response(response)
            if not isinstance(ordered_indices_raw, list):
                raise ValueError("LLM output is not a list")

            ordered_indices = []
            seen_indices = set()
            for entry in ordered_indices_raw:
                idx = entry if isinstance(entry, int) else int(str(entry).split("#")[0].strip())
                if not (0 <= idx < num_abstractions):
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid index {idx} in ordered list.")
                if idx in seen_indices:
                    raise ValueError(f"Duplicate index {idx} found in ordered list.")
                ordered_indices.append(idx)
                seen_indices.add(idx)

            if len(ordered_indices) != num_abstractions:
                raise ValueError(f"Ordered list length does not match abstractions count.")
            return ordered_indices
        except Exception as e:
            llm_logger.error(f"[Node {self.__class__.__name__}] Error: {e}", exc_info=True)
            raise e

exec parses the sequence returned by the LLM and enforces permutation validity: all indices must be within range, contain no duplicates, and match the total count of identified abstractions (len(ordered_indices) == num_abstractions).

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: list, exec_res_list: list) -> None:

Description: Stores generated chapter texts into shared["chapters"], writes .doc_cache_manifest.json if incremental mode is active, and cleans up instance state.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared pipeline state dictionary. * prep_res (list): List of items prepared by prep(). * exec_res_list (list): List of result dictionaries from all batch executions.

Returns: * None

Example: 

    def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):
        import json
        import os

        # exec_res_list contains dicts with content and hashes
        shared["chapters"] = [res["content"] for res in exec_res_list]

        # Save MD5 incremental manifest if enabled
        if shared.get("incremental"):
            output_dir = os.path.join(shared.get("output_dir", "output"), shared.get("project_name"))
            os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
            manifest_path = os.path.join(output_dir, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")

            manifest = {}
            if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
                try:
                    with open(manifest_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                        manifest = json.load(f)
                except Exception:
                    pass

            for res in exec_res_list:
                if res.get("hash") and res.get("name"):
                    manifest[res["name"]] = res["hash"]

            with open(manifest_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)

        del self.chapters_written_so_far
        del self.chapter_summaries
        print(f"Finished writing {len(exec_res_list)} chapters.")

The method extracts the content strings from all batch results into shared["chapters"]. If incremental is enabled, it updates the .doc_cache_manifest.json file with the new abstraction hashes. Finally, it deletes temporary instance attributes to free memory.

docs.title: utils.call_llm
docs.text:
Original Source File: utils/call_llm.py

The utils.call_llm module serves as the centralized Large Language Model (LLM) interaction layer for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. It provides an abstraction over multiple backend model providers, supporting the Google GenAI SDK (Vertex AI and Gemini Developer API) as well as OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoints (such as OpenRouter and Ollama). The module also encapsulates disk-backed caching mechanisms, per-run file-based structured logging, token estimation logging via utils.token_utils, dynamic model context length resolution, and configurable reasoning/thinking effort budgets.

docs.title: Architecture and Invocation Lifecycle
docs.text:
The module dispatches LLM calls through a unified entrypoint (call_llm). Depending on environment configuration, requests are routed either to Google's GenAI client library or to custom OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints, with transparent JSON caching and execution telemetry.

flowchart TD
    subgraph ClientInvocation[Invocation and Cache Evaluation]
        A["call_llm(prompt, use_cache, thinking_level)"] --> B{"use_cache == True?"}
        B -- Yes --> C["load_cache()"]
        C --> D{"prompt in cache?"}
        D -- Hit --> E["Return cached response"]
        D -- Miss --> F["get_llm_provider()"]
        B -- No --> F
    end

    subgraph ProviderRouting[Provider Routing and Execution]
        F --> G{"Provider == 'GEMINI'?"}
        G -- Yes --> H["_call_llm_gemini(prompt, thinking_level)"]
        G -- No --> I["_call_llm_provider(prompt, thinking_level)"]

        H --> H1["genai.Client(vertexai or api_key)"]
        H1 --> H2["models.generate_content(...)"]

        I --> I1{"Provider Type"}
        I1 -- OPENROUTER --> I2["Query _get_openrouter_model_info"]
        I1 -- OLLAMA --> I3["Attach think / reasoning_effort"]
        I2 --> I4["requests.post /v1/chat/completions"]
        I3 --> I4
    end

    subgraph Finalization[Response Handling and Persistence]
        H2 --> J["Extract text parts from candidates"]
        I4 --> K["Validate and extract choices[0]"]
        J --> L{"use_cache == True?"}
        K --> L
        L -- Yes --> M["save_cache(cache)"]
        L -- No --> N["Return response_text"]
        M --> N
    end

docs.title: Module-Level State and Configuration
docs.text:
The module maintains module-level state for logging, disk-backed cache file reference, and memoization of remote model capabilities:

  • logger (logging.Logger): Dedicated logger instance named "llm_logger". Initialized with a logging.NullHandler and propagate = False to prevent unconfigured root logging prior to explicit configuration via configure_logging().
  • cache_file (str): File path "llm_cache.json" where prompt-response key-value pairs are stored when caching is enabled.
  • _openrouter_models_cache (list[dict] | None): In-memory cache holding metadata returned from the OpenRouter API (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models) to prevent redundant network requests during reasoning capability verification.

docs.title: configure_logging()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial") -> str:

Description: Configures file-based logging for an execution run. It resolves the output directory from the LOG_DIR environment variable (defaulting to "logs"), sanitizes the project and mode strings for filesystem compatibility, generates a timestamped log filename, clears pre-existing handlers (such as the default NullHandler), and attaches a logging.FileHandler with UTF-8 encoding. Initial header metadata describing the run parameters is written to the log immediately upon handler creation.

Parameters: * project_name (str, optional): The name of the codebase or target project being processed. Defaults to "project". * mode (str, optional): The operating mode of the application (e.g., "tutorial", "deep-dive"). Defaults to "tutorial".

Returns: * str: The absolute or relative file path to the newly configured log file.

Raises: * OSError: If the target log directory cannot be created or the log file cannot be opened for writing.

Example: 

def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial"):
    log_directory = os.getenv("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    os.makedirs(log_directory, exist_ok=True)

    # Sanitize project name for filesystem safety
    safe_project = "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in project_name)
    safe_mode = mode.replace("-", "_")
    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    log_file = os.path.join(log_directory, f"{safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{timestamp}.log")

    # Remove any existing handlers (e.g., NullHandler) and add the file handler
    logger.handlers.clear()
    file_handler = logging.FileHandler(log_file, encoding="utf-8")
    file_handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s"))
    logger.addHandler(file_handler)

    # Log run metadata at the start of every log file
    logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")
    logger.info(f"RUN STARTED | project={project_name} | mode={mode} | timestamp={timestamp}")
    logger.info(f"Log file: {log_file}")
    logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")

    return log_file

configure_logging ensures isolated per-run logging across execution pipelines. Handlers attached to logger are cleared to avoid duplicate outputs across multiple pipeline invocations within the same process. Characters not matching alphanumeric tokens, hyphens, underscores, or periods are replaced with underscores to prevent directory traversal or invalid filename issues across operating systems.

Visibility: Public Signature: def load_cache() -> dict:

Description: Reads and deserializes the local JSON cache file designated by cache_file. If the file does not exist, cannot be read, or contains malformed JSON, the function intercepts the exception, logs a warning message to logger, and returns an empty dictionary.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary mapping prompt strings to cached model completion strings.

            return json.load(f)
    except:
        logger.warning("Failed to load cache.")

This function implements safe fallback semantics. When cold-starting without a pre-existing cache file or when reading corrupted JSON data, execution proceeds smoothly without interrupting downstream generation nodes.

Visibility: Public Signature: def save_cache(cache: dict) -> None:

Description: Serializes the provided cache dictionary to the local file designated by cache_file in JSON format. Any I/O errors encountered during the write operation are caught and recorded as warnings in the logging pipeline.
