docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_llm_provider() -> str | None:

Description: Determines the active LLM backend provider based on ambient environment variables. It inspects LLM_PROVIDER, falling back to "GEMINI" if LLM_PROVIDER is unset but GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY is present.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * str | None: The identifier string of the provider (e.g., "GEMINI", "OPENROUTER", "OLLAMA"), or None if no relevant configuration is detected.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def get_llm_provider():
    provider = os.getenv("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if not provider and (os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") or os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY")):
        provider = "GEMINI"
    # if necessary, add ANTHROPIC/OPENAI
    return provider

This helper centralizes provider resolution rules so that Google Gemini remains the default provider whenever Google credentials are present, while allowing explicit overrides via the LLM_PROVIDER environment variable.

docs.title: _get_openrouter_model_info()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _get_openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict | None:

Description: Retrieves capability and parameter metadata for a specified OpenRouter model identifier by querying the OpenRouter models catalog endpoint (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models). The response payload is cached in the module-level variable _openrouter_models_cache to avoid repeated remote API requests on subsequent lookups.

Parameters: * model_id (str): The full identifier of the model (e.g., "anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet").

Returns: * dict | None: The dictionary containing model metadata (such as context length and reasoning effort configurations) if found; otherwise None.

Raises: * None. Network errors during the HTTP request are caught, resulting in an empty model cache.

Example: 

def _get_openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict:
    global _openrouter_models_cache
    if _openrouter_models_cache is None:
        try:
            resp = requests.get("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models", timeout=5)
            _openrouter_models_cache = resp.json().get("data", [])
        except Exception:
            _openrouter_models_cache = []

    return next((m for m in _openrouter_models_cache if m.get("id") == model_id), None)

The function applies a memoization strategy over the global _openrouter_models_cache. If network failures or timeouts occur during the request, the cache is initialized to an empty list, allowing fallback defaults to take effect downstream.

docs.title: get_model_context_length()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:

Description: Determines the maximum token context window supported by a given model based on the endpoint URL and model name. If the endpoint corresponds to Google Gemini (generativelanguage.googleapis.com or if "gemini" is in model_name), it returns a default limit of 1,000,000 tokens. If the endpoint points to OpenRouter (openrouter.ai), it queries the OpenRouter models API to extract the exact context_length attribute. For other providers or in the event of an error, it returns a standard fallback limit of 100,000 tokens.

Parameters: * endpoint_url (str): The base or complete endpoint URL of the model service. * model_name (str): The model identifier string. * api_key (str, optional): The API key for authenticated requests. Defaults to "".

Returns: * int: The maximum token context length allowed for prompt construction.

Raises: * None. Catches all exceptions internally and logs a warning message.

Example: 

def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:
    default_limit = 100000
    try:
        if not endpoint_url:
            return default_limit

        if "generativelanguage.googleapis.com" in endpoint_url or "gemini" in model_name.lower():
            # Safely default to 1M tokens for Gemini models
            return 1000000

        if "openrouter.ai" in endpoint_url:
            resp = requests.get("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models", timeout=5)
            data = resp.json().get("data", [])
            for m in data:
                if m.get("id") == model_name:
                    return m.get("context_length", default_limit)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch context length for {model_name} at {endpoint_url}: {e}")

    return default_limit

This context discovery helper assists document ingestion and prompt construction nodes by preventing token overflow exceptions before payloads are submitted to target providers.

docs.title: _call_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Executes an HTTP POST request against an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions API endpoint determined by dynamic environment variables (e.g., OLLAMA_* or OPENROUTER_*). It constructs the authorization headers, sets temperature parameters, configures reasoning/thinking effort payloads according to provider capabilities, and executes the request with strict connection and read timeouts ((10, 300)). The response is parsed to verify JSON validity and defensively checked for the existence of non-empty choices elements.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The user prompt to send to the completion endpoint. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Desired reasoning effort (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The completion text extracted from choices[0]["message"]["content"].

Raises: * ValueError: If required environment variables (LLM_PROVIDER, <provider>_MODEL, <provider>_BASE_URL) are missing, if invalid JSON is returned by the provider, or if the response JSON lacks the choices key. * Exception: Wraps underlying requests.exceptions.HTTPError, requests.exceptions.ConnectionError, requests.exceptions.Timeout, or general requests.exceptions.RequestException with descriptive context.

Example: 

def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    # Read the provider from environment variable
    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if not provider:
        raise ValueError("LLM_PROVIDER environment variable is required")

    # Construct the names of the other environment variables
    model_var = f"{provider}_MODEL"
    base_url_var = f"{provider}_BASE_URL"
    api_key_var = f"{provider}_API_KEY"

    model = os.environ.get(model_var)
    base_url = os.environ.get(base_url_var)
    api_key = os.environ.get(api_key_var, "")

    if not model:
        raise ValueError(f"{model_var} environment variable is required")
    if not base_url:
        raise ValueError(f"{base_url_var} environment variable is required")

    url = f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/chat/completions"
    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
    if api_key:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"

    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        "temperature": 0.7,
    }

    if provider == "OPENROUTER" and thinking_level:
        model_info = _get_openrouter_model_info(model)
        if model_info and "reasoning" in model_info:
            supported_efforts = model_info["reasoning"].get("supported_efforts", [])
            if thinking_level.lower() in supported_efforts:
                payload["reasoning"] = {"effort": thinking_level.lower()}
                payload["temperature"] = 1.0
            else:
                logger.warning(f"Invalid thinking level '{thinking_level}' for model {model}. Supported efforts: {supported_efforts}")
        else:
            logger.warning(f"Model {model} does not support reasoning via OpenRouter API.")

    elif provider == "OLLAMA" and thinking_level:
        payload["think"] = thinking_level.lower()
        payload["reasoning_effort"] = thinking_level.lower()
        payload["temperature"] = 1.0

    try:
        response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=(10, 300))
        # ... JSON parsing, defensive choices validation, and HTTP status verification ...
        response_json = response.json()
        response.raise_for_status()

        if "choices" not in response_json or not response_json["choices"]:
            error_detail = response_json.get("error", response_json)
            logger.warning(f"API returned 200 but no 'choices' in response: {error_detail}")
            raise ValueError(f"API response missing 'choices' key. Response: {error_detail}")

        return response_json["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
    except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as e:
        # ... Detailed error extraction ...
        raise Exception(error_message) from e

_call_llm_provider dynamically composes request schemas based on target provider rules. When provider == "OPENROUTER" and reasoning is requested, it queries _get_openrouter_model_info() to validate that the model's reasoning.supported_efforts includes the requested level. If supported, payload["reasoning"] = {"effort": ...} is attached and temperature is shifted to 1.0 (as required by reasoning models). For OLLAMA, both think and reasoning_effort fields are injected to maintain compatibility across various Ollama server releases.

docs.title: _call_llm_gemini()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Executes a content generation request using the official google-genai SDK client (google.genai.Client). It authenticates via Vertex AI if GEMINI_PROJECT_ID is set (using GEMINI_LOCATION with a default of "us-central1"), or via Gemini Developer API key if GEMINI_API_KEY is present. When a thinking_level is specified, it maps the level string ("low", "medium", "high") to a corresponding token budget (1024, 4096, 8192) and constructs a types.GenerateContentConfig with types.ThinkingConfig(include_thoughts=True, thinking_budget=budget). The resulting content parts are filtered to concatenate only non-null text components, safely stripping thought signatures and metadata.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The user prompt text. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Desired thinking budget level ("low", "medium", or "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The concatenated text returned in the model candidate response. Returns an empty string if no candidates or text parts exist.

Raises: * ValueError: If neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY is present in the environment.

Example: 

def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
        client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"), location=os.getenv("GEMINI_LOCATION", "us-central1"))
    elif os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        client = genai.Client(api_key=os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"))
    else:
        raise ValueError("Either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY must be set in the environment")
    model = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")

    kwargs = {"model": model, "contents": [prompt]}

    if thinking_level:
        # Map string levels to budgets for the installed SDK version
        budget_map = {"low": 1024, "medium": 4096, "high": 8192}
        budget = budget_map.get(thinking_level.lower(), 4096)
        thinking_config = types.ThinkingConfig(include_thoughts=True, thinking_budget=budget)
        kwargs["config"] = types.GenerateContentConfig(thinking_config=thinking_config)

    response = client.models.generate_content(**kwargs)

    # Extract only text parts to avoid "non-text parts: ['thought_signature']" warnings
    if response.candidates and response.candidates[0].content.parts:
        text_parts = [part.text for part in response.candidates[0].content.parts if part.text is not None]
        return "".join(text_parts)
    return ""

By filtering response content parts (part.text is not None), _call_llm_gemini avoids SDK warnings when reasoning is enabled, as reasoning models (such as Gemini 2.5/3.7 with thinking enabled) include binary or non-text thought signatures in response candidate parts.

docs.title: call_llm()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Primary public entry point for dispatching prompts to LLMs. It calculates estimated prompt token counts using utils.token_utils.count_tokens, records structured logs of the request metadata, checks and returns cached responses when use_cache is True, routes uncached requests to the configured provider implementation (_call_llm_gemini or _call_llm_provider), updates the persistent disk cache, logs request execution timings, and returns the completion text.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The full text prompt to be submitted to the LLM. * use_cache (bool, optional): Whether to check and update the local JSON cache (llm_cache.json). Defaults to True. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning effort level ("low", "medium", "high", or None). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The completion text generated by the model.

Raises: * ValueError: If required environment variables are absent or response schemas are invalid. * Exception: If provider API requests fail, time out, or encounter network errors.

Example: 

def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    import time

    from utils.token_utils import count_tokens

    provider = get_llm_provider()
    model = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL", "unknown"))
    prompt_tokens = count_tokens(prompt)

    logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")
    logger.info(
        f"LLM CALL START | provider={provider} | model={model} | thinking={thinking_level} | cache={'enabled' if use_cache else 'disabled'} | prompt_tokens={prompt_tokens:,}"
    )
    logger.info(f"PROMPT:\n{prompt}")

    # Check cache if enabled
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        if prompt in cache:
            cached_response = cache[prompt]
            logger.info(f"CACHE HIT | response_chars={len(cached_response):,}")
            logger.info(f"RESPONSE (cached):\n{cached_response}")
            logger.info("LLM CALL END | result=cache_hit")
            return cached_response

    # Make the actual LLM call
    start_time = time.time()
    logger.info(f"API CALL | sending request to {provider}...")

    if provider == "GEMINI":
        response_text = _call_llm_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
    else:  # generic method using a URL that is OpenAI compatible API (Ollama, ...)
        response_text = _call_llm_provider(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)

    elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    logger.info(f"API CALL COMPLETE | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | response_chars={len(response_text):,}")
    logger.info(f"RESPONSE:\n{response_text}")

    # Update cache if enabled
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        cache[prompt] = response_text
        save_cache(cache)
        logger.info("CACHE WRITE | saved response to cache")

    logger.info(f"LLM CALL END | result=success | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s")
    return response_text

The function orchestrates logging, caching, token accounting, and provider dispatch. By importing count_tokens from utils.token_utils at runtime, it maintains token awareness in logging streams without introducing circular dependencies during initial module loading.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The utils.crawl_github_files module provides comprehensive crawling and extraction mechanisms for remote GitHub repositories. It serves as one of the primary ingestion pipelines for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. The module supports two primary ingestion pathways:

  1. SSH Git Clone Path: Triggered when the repository URL uses SSH syntax (starts with git@ or ends with .git). It clones the remote repository to a local temporary directory via GitPython (git.Repo.clone_from), parses any top-level .gitignore via pathspec, evaluates glob pattern inclusions/exclusions, and reads matching text files from disk.
  2. GitHub REST API Path: Triggered for standard GitHub HTTP/HTTPS URLs (including tree/branch/subdirectory URLs). It communicates directly with the GitHub REST API v3 to inspect commits, resolve branches/trees, download repository trees, handle API rate limiting with automatic sleep/retry backoff, and retrieve file contents via direct download URLs or base64-encoded JSON blobs.

Both pathways normalize results into a dictionary mapping relative file paths to their raw string contents, along with metadata statistics describing total processed, excluded, and skipped files.

flowchart TD
    Start([repo_url]) --> CheckSSH{Is SSH URL?<br/>git@ or .git}

    subgraph SSH_Workflow [SSH Clone Strategy]
        CheckSSH -- Yes --> TempDir[Create Temporary Directory]
        TempDir --> GitClone[git.Repo.clone_from]
        GitClone --> LoadGitIgnoreSSH[Parse .gitignore via PathSpec]
        LoadGitIgnoreSSH --> WalkDisk[os.walk directory]
        WalkDisk --> FilterSSH{Filter Inclusion / Exclusion / Size / Text}
        FilterSSH --> ReadDisk[Read file with utf-8-sig]
    end

    subgraph API_Workflow [GitHub REST API Strategy]
        CheckSSH -- No --> ParseURL[Parse URL: Owner, Repo, Tree, Path]
        ParseURL --> ResolveRef[Resolve Branch or Tree SHA via API]
        ResolveRef --> FetchGitIgnoreAPI[Fetch .gitignore via API]
        FetchGitIgnoreAPI --> RecurseAPI[Recursive fetch_contents]
        RecurseAPI --> FetchItem{Item Type}
        FetchItem -- dir --> CheckDirFilter{Filter Directory}
        CheckDirFilter -- Pass --> RecurseAPI
        FetchItem -- file --> FilterAPI{Filter Inclusion / Exclusion / Size}
        FilterAPI -- Pass --> DownloadFile[Download Raw URL or Base64]
    end

    ReadDisk --> ReturnDict([Return files and stats dict])
    DownloadFile --> ReturnDict

    include_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None,
    exclude_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None,

Description: Crawls files from a specified GitHub repository URL at a specific commit, branch, or subfolder path. The function parses input parameters, standardizes pattern sets, and branches into either an SSH cloning workflow or an HTTP REST API traversal workflow based on the structure of repo_url.

During execution, the function enforces file inclusion patterns (include_patterns), exclusion rules (exclude_patterns), gitignore rules (via pathspec), and maximum file size thresholds (max_file_size). It logs formatted, ANSI-colorized status messages to stdout during file evaluation and returns a consolidated dictionary with downloaded contents and execution statistics.

Parameters: * repo_url (str): URL of the GitHub repository. docs.text:

def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether a specific file should be accepted for processing based on glob patterns and Git ignore specifications. The function checks three consecutive filtering stages: 1. Validates the file_name against include_patterns (if defined) using fnmatch.fnmatch. 2. Evaluates the full relative file_path against gitignore_spec via pathspec.PathSpec.match_file. 3. Evaluates the full relative file_path against exclude_patterns (if defined) using fnmatch.fnmatch.

Parameters: * file_path (str): The relative path of the file within the repository. * file_name (str): The base name of the file (e.g., main.py). * gitignore_spec (pathspec.PathSpec | None, optional): A compiled PathSpec instance containing gitignore wildmatch rules. Defaults to None.

Returns: * bool: True if the file passes inclusion checks and does not hit gitignore or exclusion rules; False otherwise.

Core Implementation: 

    def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:
        """Determine if a file should be included based on patterns"""
        # If no include patterns are specified, include all files
        if not include_patterns:
            include_file = True
        else:
            # Check if file matches any include pattern
            include_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_name, pattern) for pattern in include_patterns)

        # Check gitignore if provided
        if include_file and gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path):
            return False

        # If exclude patterns are specified, check if file should be excluded
        if exclude_patterns and include_file:
            # Exclude if file matches any exclude pattern
            exclude_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, pattern) for pattern in exclude_patterns)
            return not exclude_file

        return include_file

The matching precedence enforces that files must first satisfy positive inclusion criteria before negative exclusion criteria are evaluated. Notice that include_patterns matches strictly against the base file_name, whereas gitignore_spec and exclude_patterns evaluate against the full relative file_path. This allows users to include all *.py files while excluding nested subdirectories matching tests/*.

def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str) -> list[dict]:

Description: Queries the GitHub API endpoint GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches to list all branches available in the target repository. This is used during URL parsing to determine if a /tree/<ref>/... URL component refers to a named branch (including branches with slashes in their names such as feature/auth).

Parameters: * owner (str): The GitHub account or organization name. * repo (str): The GitHub repository name.

Returns: * list[dict]: A list of branch metadata dictionaries returned by the GitHub REST API. Returns an empty list [] on HTTP error status codes (404, etc.).

Raises: * Exception: If HTTP status 403 or 429 is received without an authenticated token, indicating API rate limit exhaustion.

Core Implementation: 

    def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str):
        """Get brancshes of the repository"""

        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches"
        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")

        if response.status_code == 404:
            if not token:
                print(
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or is private.\n"
                    "If this is a private repository, please provide a valid GitHub token via the 'token' argument or set the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable."
                )
            else:
                print(
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or insufficient permissions with the provided token.\n"
                    "Please verify the repository exists and the token has access to this repository."
                )
            return []

        if response.status_code != 200:
            print(f"Error fetching the branches of {owner}/{repo}: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")
            return []

        return response.json()

The function incorporates custom handling for HTTP 404 and rate limiting errors. When an unauthenticated client receives a rate limit status (403 or 429), an explicit exception is raised advising the user to pass a token. For 404 errors, diagnostic messages distinguish between missing private repository credentials and missing public resources.

docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Closure Helper) Signature: 

def fetch_contents(path: str) -> None:

Description: Recursively traverses repository folders and retrieves file contents via GitHub's Contents API (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}). It handles directory recursion, exclusion pruning, rate limit backoff, size validation, and content decoding.

sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Crawler as fetch_contents(path)
    participant GH_API as GitHub Contents API
    participant RawHost as Raw Download Host

    Crawler->>GH_API: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}?ref={ref}
    alt HTTP 403 / 429 Rate Limit
        GH_API-->>Crawler: Rate limit response + X-RateLimit-Reset
        Crawler->>Crawler: sleep(wait_time)
        Crawler->>GH_API: Retry GET /contents/{path}
    end
    GH_API-->>Crawler: JSON response (file item or dir list)

    loop For each item in response
        alt item[type] == 'dir'
            Crawler->>Crawler: Evaluate dir against exclude_patterns & .gitignore
            opt Not Excluded
                Crawler->>Crawler: fetch_contents(item[path])
            end
        else item[type] == 'file'
            Crawler->>Crawler: should_include_file(rel_path, name)
            opt File Included & Size <= max_file_size
                alt item[download_url] exists
                    Crawler->>RawHost: GET item[download_url]
                    RawHost-->>Crawler: Raw text
                    Crawler->>Crawler: Store in files[rel_path]
                else base64 content in payload
                    Crawler->>Crawler: base64.b64decode(content)
                    Crawler->>Crawler: Store in files[rel_path]
                end
            end
        end
    end

Parameters: * path (str): Repository directory path to inspect. An empty string ("") targets the repository root.

Returns: * None: Mutates the enclosing files, api_counters, api_skipped_size, and api_skipped_non_text data structures directly.

Raises: * Exception: If rate limits are exceeded while unauthenticated.

Core Implementation: 

    def fetch_contents(path):
        """Fetch contents of the repository at a specific path and commit"""
        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}"
        params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}

        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and "rate limit exceeded" in response.text.lower():
            if not token:
                raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")
            reset_time = int(response.headers.get("X-RateLimit-Reset", 0))
            wait_time = max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1
            print(f"Rate limit exceeded. Waiting for {wait_time:.0f} seconds...")
            time.sleep(wait_time)
            return fetch_contents(path)

        # ... [HTTP 404 / error checks] ...

        contents = response.json()
        if not isinstance(contents, list):
            contents = [contents]

        for item in contents:
            item_path = item["path"]
            # ... [Relative path normalization] ...

            if item["type"] == "file":
                # ... [Pattern check, size check, download_url or base64 decode] ...
                if item.get("download_url"):
                    file_response = requests.get(item["download_url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
                    if file_response.status_code == 200:
                        files[rel_path] = file_response.text
                        api_counters["processed"] += 1
                # ... [Base64 fallback branch] ...
            elif item["type"] == "dir":
                # ... [Directory exclusion checks] ...
                fetch_contents(item_path)

fetch_contents implements rate-limit recovery. If authenticated requests trigger GitHub's secondary or primary rate limits, it extracts the X-RateLimit-Reset epoch timestamp, calculates the required sleep delta using time.time(), pauses the thread via time.sleep(), and retries the call. For files, raw content is fetched from download_url if present, falling back to decoding base64 inline content strings from the API response payload.

docs.text:
Original File Path: utils/crawl_local_files.py

This module is the local filesystem counterpart to utils.crawl_github_files. It extracts, filters, and loads text file contents from a local directory tree into an in-memory dictionary.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The primary responsibility of utils.crawl_local_files is to traverse a directory hierarchy on the local filesystem, evaluate files and directories against exclusion rules and ignore files, filter candidate items based on include patterns and byte size limits, and parse valid text files into memory.

Key features and execution characteristics include: 1. .gitignore Integration: Automatically searches for a root .gitignore file within the specified directory and compiles its rules into a pathspec.PathSpec matcher using the gitwildmatch pattern grammar. 2. Directory Pruning: Inspects subdirectories during traversal and removes excluded directories from dirs in-place within os.walk, preventing recursive traversal into ignored subtrees (such as .venv, __pycache__, or .git). 3. Multi-Stage File Filtering: Filters individual files in a structured sequence: .gitignore matching, explicit exclude_patterns, positive matching against include_patterns, and maximum file size thresholds (max_file_size). 4. Encoding & Binary Safety: Reads files using utf-8-sig encoding (handling UTF-8 with or without Byte Order Mark) and traps UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, and other I/O exceptions to skip non-text or binary files cleanly. 5. Console Progress Telemetry: Outputs formatted ANSI-colored log lines for every evaluated path along with an aggregate execution summary upon completion.

docs.title: crawl_local_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def crawl_local_files(directory, include_patterns=None, exclude_patterns=None, max_file_size=None, use_relative_paths=True)

Description: Traverses the specified directory path using os.walk, applying exclusion and inclusion matching logic against directories and files. The function parses and enforces root .gitignore files via pathspec, enforces size limits on candidate files, reads UTF-8 text contents, and generates console output detailing the status of every file and directory encountered.

docs.title: Core Implementation:
docs.text:
def crawl_local_files(
    directory,
    include_patterns=None,
    exclude_patterns=None,
    max_file_size=None,
    use_relative_paths=True,
):
    if not os.path.isdir(directory):
        raise ValueError(f"Directory does not exist: {directory}")

    files_dict = {}

    # --- ANSI colors ---
    C_GREEN = "\033[92m"
    C_GRAY = "\033[90m"
    C_RED = "\033[91m"
    C_RESET = "\033[0m"

    # --- Counters ---
    entry_num = 0
    count_processed = 0
    count_excluded = 0
    count_size_limit = 0
    count_non_text = 0
    skipped_size_limit = []
    skipped_non_text = []

    # --- Load .gitignore ---
    gitignore_path = os.path.join(directory, ".gitignore")
    gitignore_spec = None
    if os.path.exists(gitignore_path):
        try:
            with open(gitignore_path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                gitignore_patterns = f.readlines()
            gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", gitignore_patterns)
            print(f"Loaded .gitignore patterns from {gitignore_path}")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Warning: Could not read or parse .gitignore file {gitignore_path}: {e}")

    # ... [Directory and File Filtering Logic] ...

The function first verifies that the target directory exists and is a directory; if not, it immediately raises a ValueError. It initializes tracking counters for processed files, excluded paths, size-exceeded files, and non-text/binary files. Next, it checks for a .gitignore file located at the root of directory. If present, it loads all lines and compiles a pathspec.PathSpec instance using the gitwildmatch rule set. If reading or compiling the .gitignore fails, it logs a warning message to standard output and continues execution with gitignore_spec set to None.

docs.title: Directory Pruning Logic:
docs.text:
# --- Single-pass: walk, filter, and process inline ---
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(directory):
        # --- Directory filtering ---
        excluded_dirs = set()
        for d in sorted(dirs):
            dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), directory)

            reason = None
            if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
                reason = "excluded (.gitignore)"
            elif exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    dir_pattern = pattern[:-2] if pattern.endswith("/*") else pattern
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                        reason = "excluded"
                        break

            if reason:
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                entry_num += 1
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {dirpath_rel}/ [{reason}]{C_RESET}")

        for d in dirs.copy():
            if d in excluded_dirs:
                dirs.remove(d)

        # Sort remaining dirs for consistent traversal order
        dirs.sort()

        # ... [File Processing Loop] ...

During each step of os.walk, subdirectories in dirs are evaluated before entering them. For every directory name d, the relative path from directory is computed. If gitignore_spec matches the relative directory path, or if exclude_patterns match the relative directory path or folder name directly (with trailing /* wildcard suffixes stripped), the directory is added to excluded_dirs. The excluded entries are then removed in-place from dirs using dirs.remove(d). This mutates the active list used by os.walk, pruning entire directory trees from subsequent traversal and avoiding redundant filesystem operations.

docs.title: File Processing and Reading Logic:
docs.text:
# --- File processing (inline, sorted) ---
        for filename in sorted(files):
            filepath = os.path.join(root, filename)
            relpath = os.path.relpath(filepath, directory) if use_relative_paths else filepath
            entry_num += 1

            # Check gitignore
            if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(relpath):
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [excluded (.gitignore)]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            # Check exclude patterns
            excluded = False
            if exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(relpath, pattern):
                        excluded = True
                        break
            if excluded:
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [excluded]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            # Check include patterns
            if include_patterns:
                matched = False
                for pattern in include_patterns:
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(relpath, pattern):
                        matched = True
                        break
                if not matched:
                    count_excluded += 1
                    print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [excluded (not in include list)]{C_RESET}")
                    continue

            # Check size limit
            if max_file_size and os.path.getsize(filepath) > max_file_size:
                count_size_limit += 1
                skipped_size_limit.append(relpath)
                size_kb = os.path.getsize(filepath) / 1024
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [size limit: {size_kb:.0f}KB]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            # Try to read as text
            try:
                with open(filepath, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                files_dict[relpath] = content
                count_processed += 1
                print(f"{C_GREEN}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [processed]{C_RESET}")
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [cannot process: not a text file]{C_RESET}")
            except Exception as e:
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [cannot process: {e}]{C_RESET}")

Files within retained directories are processed in sorted order. For each file, the path key is calculated as relative or absolute based on use_relative_paths. The file is checked against gitignore_spec, exclude_patterns, and include_patterns. If all filter checks pass, the byte size is validated against max_file_size. If valid, the file is opened with encoding="utf-8-sig". If the content fails to decode (raising UnicodeDecodeError or ValueError), the error is caught, the file is categorized as non-text, and execution continues without crashing.

docs.title: Reporting and Output Summary:
docs.text:
# --- Summary ---
    total_fetched = count_processed + count_excluded + count_size_limit + count_non_text
    print("\n--- Crawl Summary ---")
    print(f"  Total found : {total_fetched}")
    print(f"{C_GREEN}  Processed   : {count_processed}{C_RESET}")
    if count_excluded > 0:
        print(f"{C_GRAY}  Excluded    : {count_excluded}{C_RESET}")
    if count_size_limit > 0:
        print(f"{C_RED}  Size limit  : {count_size_limit}{C_RESET}")
        for f in skipped_size_limit:
            print(f"{C_RED}    - {f}{C_RESET}")
    if count_non_text > 0:
        print(f"{C_RED}  Non-text    : {count_non_text}{C_RESET}")
        for f in skipped_non_text:
            print(f"{C_RED}    - {f}{C_RESET}")
    print("---------------------")

    return {"files": files_dict}

Once the filesystem walk is complete, the function tallies the total entries encountered and prints a summary block highlighting the count of processed, excluded, size-limited, and non-text files using ANSI color codes (C_GREEN, C_GRAY, C_RED, C_RESET). The resulting dictionary is returned in the format {"files": {filepath: content}}.

Parameters: * directory (str): The root path to the local directory to be traversed. * include_patterns (set or None): Optional collection of glob patterns that files must match (e.g., {"*.py", "*.js"}). If None, no include filtering is applied. * exclude_patterns (set or None): Optional collection of glob patterns for files and directories to exclude (e.g., {"tests/*", "*.pyc"}). * max_file_size (int or None): Maximum allowed file size in bytes. Files exceeding this threshold are skipped. * use_relative_paths (bool): Whether the dictionary keys returned in "files" should be paths relative to directory (True) or full filesystem paths (False). Defaults to True.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary containing a single key "files", which maps file path strings to their decoded text content strings: 

{
    "files": {
        "utils/crawl_local_files.py": "import fnmatch...",
        "README.md": "# Project Title..."
    }
}

Raises: * ValueError: Raised if directory does not exist or is not a valid directory (not os.path.isdir(directory)).

Example: 

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("--- Crawling parent directory ('..') ---")
    files_data = crawl_local_files(
        "..",
        exclude_patterns={
            "*.pyc",
            "__pycache__/*",
            ".venv/*",
            ".git/*",
            "docs/*",
            "output/*",
        },
    )
    print(f"Found {len(files_data['files'])} files:")
    for path in files_data["files"]:
        print(f"  {path}")

The generated prompt instructs the language model to inspect an indexed list of repository files and identify which files represent actual executable code modules (defining APIs, functions, classes, and business logic) versus non-code artifacts such as UI markup, configuration, static assets, and build system manifests. The prompt explicitly demands output formatted strictly as a YAML list of file indices.

Parameters: * project_name (str): The name of the target repository or project being documented. * file_listing (str): A pre-formatted, indexed list of all discovered files in the project codebase (e.g., lines containing index numbers and file paths).

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name: str, file_listing: str) -> str:
    """Build the prompt for DeterministicFileMapper to filter non-code files.

    Used in api-reference mode to identify which files are actual code modules
    (APIs, functions, classes, business logic) vs. UI layouts, configs, assets.
    """
    return (
        f"For the project `{project_name}`, here is the list of all files in the codebase:\n\n"
        f"{file_listing}\n\n"
        f"Your task is to identify WHICH of these files are ACTUAL CODE files that contain "
        f"APIs, functions, classes, or core business logic.\n"
        f"EXCLUDE: UI layouts (like .xaml, .storyboard, .html), configuration files "
        f"(like .xml, .json, .manifest, .ini), static assets, build scripts "
        f"(like .csproj, .sln), and documentation.\n\n"
        f"Return ONLY a YAML list of the file indices that should be documented as code modules.\n\n"
        f"```yaml\n- 0\n- 1\n- 3\n```"
    )

The prompt generated by build_code_file_filter_prompt guides the LLM to output pure YAML arrays of integer indices corresponding to the input file_listing. By establishing strict exclusion criteria (e.g., eliminating .xaml, .storyboard, .xml, .json, .csproj, and .sln files), it optimizes token utilization and prevents non-logic files from consuming generation budget in downstream API reference passes. Downstream callers parse the returned fenced YAML block directly into a list of integers to slice the master file collection.

Visibility: Public Signature: def build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num: int, abstraction_name: str, chapter_content: str, language: str = "english") -> str:

Description: Assembles a structured prompt to generate a technical summary of a newly generated documentation chapter. This summary is injected into subsequent chapter prompts to maintain cross-chapter coherence and track architectural state across large document generations. The prompt enforces a uniform 4-dimension technical brief (Scope & Responsibility, Key Technical Elements, Implementation Patterns & Architecture, System Integration & Dependencies), requiring 3 to 5 concise technical sentences per dimension.

Parameters: * chapter_num (int): The sequence number of the chapter currently being summarized. * abstraction_name (str): The title or architectural abstraction represented by the chapter. * chapter_content (str): The raw Markdown content generated for the chapter. * language (str, optional): The target natural language for the summary output. Defaults to "english".

Returns: * str: The fully populated prompt string instructing the LLM to summarize the chapter across the 4 technical dimensions.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num: int, abstraction_name: str, chapter_content: str, language: str = "english") -> str:
    """Build the prompt for generating a technical summary of a written chapter.

    Used after each chapter is generated to create a concise technical summary
    for cross-chapter context. The summary is fed into subsequent chapters'
    prompts so the LLM maintains coherence across the full document.

    The summary captures 4 technical dimensions with 3-5 sentences each:
    1. Component scope & responsibility
    2. Key classes/services/functions and their roles
    3. Implementation patterns & architectural decisions
    4. Inter-component interfaces & dependencies
    """
    lang_instruction = f"Write the entire summary in {language.capitalize()}. " if language.lower() != "english" else ""
    return (
        f"{lang_instruction}"
        f"Summarize the following documentation chapter as a structured technical brief. "
        f"For EACH of the 4 points below, write 3-5 concise technical sentences:\n\n"
        f"(1) **Component Scope & Responsibility**: What is the main technical domain this "
        f"chapter covers? What problems does it solve and what role does it play in the system?\n\n"
        f"(2) **Key Technical Elements**: What are the specific classes, services, functions, "
        f"data models, or protocols discussed? Name them and describe their concrete roles.\n\n"
        f"(3) **Implementation Patterns & Architecture**: What design patterns, communication "
        f"protocols, data flow strategies, error handling mechanisms, or security measures "
        f"are covered? How are they implemented?\n\n"
        f"(4) **System Integration & Dependencies**: How does this component interface with "
        f"other parts of the system? What does it consume from or provide to other components? "
        f"What are the key integration points?\n\n"
        f"---\n"
        f"Chapter {chapter_num}: {abstraction_name}\n"
        f"{chapter_content}"
    )

build_chapter_summary_prompt enforces a standardized schema for inter-chapter memory. When handling multi-language documentation pipelines, the language argument prefixes the prompt with an explicit localization directive (Write the entire summary in <Language>.) whenever the selected language differs from English. The resulting 4-point structure guarantees that downstream chapter generations receive concise, high-density architectural summaries covering domain scope, concrete identifiers, implementation patterns, and dependency graphs without context overflow.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_mkdocs_config(site_name: str, nav_yaml: str) -> str:

Description: Generates a complete mkdocs.yml configuration file string configured for the mkdocs-material theme. The configuration includes code block copy buttons, Pygments syntax highlighting with line anchors, inline code highlights, and Python Markdown SuperFences configured to render Mermaid diagram definitions natively. It parses the incoming navigation YAML block and merges it under the primary nav: tree starting with Home: index.md.

Parameters: * site_name (str): The title displayed in the MkDocs header and metadata. * nav_yaml (str): A YAML snippet representing navigation items. Can include a leading nav: line, which is stripped automatically.

Returns: * str: A valid, multi-line YAML document ready to be written directly to mkdocs.yml.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def build_mkdocs_config(site_name: str, nav_yaml: str) -> str:
    """Build a complete mkdocs.yml for local --mkdocs output.

    Generates a ready-to-use MkDocs Material config with:
    - Material theme with code copy buttons
    - Syntax highlighting (pymdownx.highlight + inlinehilite)
    - Mermaid diagram rendering via pymdownx.superfences custom fences
    - Navigation from the generated nav_snippet

    Users can run `mkdocs serve` or `mkdocs build` directly in the output dir.
    """
    # Extract nav items from nav_snippet (strip the "nav:" header line)
    nav_lines = nav_yaml.split("\n")
    nav_body = "\n".join(nav_lines[1:]) if nav_lines else ""

    return (
        f"site_name: '{site_name}'\n"
        f"theme:\n"
        f"  name: material\n"
        f"  features:\n"
        f"    - content.code.copy\n"
        f"markdown_extensions:\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.highlight:\n"
        f"      anchor_linenums: true\n"
        f"      use_pygments: true\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.superfences:\n"
        f"      custom_fences:\n"
        f"        - name: mermaid\n"
        f"          class: mermaid\n"
        f"          format: !!python/name:pymdownx.superfences.fence_code_format\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.inlinehilite\n"
        f"nav:\n"
        f"  - Home: index.md\n"
        f"{nav_body}\n"
    )

The function handles YAML formatting quirks by splitting nav_yaml on newline boundaries and stripping the initial line (assuming it starts with nav:), subsequently indenting the remaining navigation structure under nav: alongside - Home: index.md. The configuration enables pymdownx.superfences with Python object resolution for fence_code_format, allowing MkDocs to natively interpret fenced ```mermaid blocks generated across the documentation pipeline.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The utils.token_utils module provides tokenization, token counting, and telemetry estimation utilities for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder pipeline. Because large language models impose strict input context window limits and cost constraints, accurate token estimation is necessary before executing graph operations and LLM prompts.

This module encapsulates lazy-loaded tiktoken encoding using a singleton pattern. When available, it leverages the cl100k_base BPE (Byte-Pair Encoding) tokenizer used by modern OpenAI architectures. If tiktoken is unavailable or encounters initialization issues, it gracefully falls back to a 4-character-per-token heuristic (len(text) // 4). Additionally, the module exposes structured logging utilities that output colorized console alerts and stream metrics into the shared llm_logger.

docs.title: _get_encoding()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private / Internal Helper Signature: def _get_encoding()

Description: Initializes and retrieves the global tiktoken BPE tokenizer instance. It uses the "cl100k_base" encoding specification. If the encoding object has not been loaded yet, it attempts instantiation within a try-except block; any failure resets or retains _encoding as None. This guarantees that tokenizer setup failures do not crash the pipeline and allow downstream fallback execution.

def _get_encoding():
    global _encoding
    if _encoding is None:
        try:
            _encoding = tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
        except Exception:
            _encoding = None
    return _encoding

_get_encoding manages the lifecycle of the tokenizer singleton across thread calls and node executions. By deferring tokenizer creation until the first token count is requested, application startup time is minimized. In containerized or sandboxed environments where tokenizer binary assets or network caches might be restricted, the broad except Exception ensures continuous operation by returning None instead of propagating uncaught exceptions.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * tiktoken.Encoding | None: The loaded cl100k_base encoding object if available, otherwise None.

Raises: * No exceptions are raised; errors during tiktoken.get_encoding are swallowed and set _encoding to None.

Example: 

# Internal usage inside utils/token_utils.py:
enc = _get_encoding()
if enc:
    return len(enc.encode(text))
return len(text) // 4

docs.title: count_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def count_tokens(text: str) -> int:

Description: Calculates the exact or estimated token count for a given string. If text is empty or falsy, it immediately returns 0. When the tiktoken encoding instance is successfully retrieved via _get_encoding(), it performs exact BPE tokenization (len(enc.encode(text))). If the tokenizer is unavailable, it applies a fast integer division heuristic based on character length (len(text) // 4).

def count_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    """Count tokens using tiktoken, with fallback to chars/4."""
    if not text:
        return 0
    enc = _get_encoding()
    if enc:
        return len(enc.encode(text))
    return len(text) // 4

This function is the primary token estimation workhorse across the framework. It handles boundary cases such as "" or None by immediately returning zero before calling the tokenizer. When exact tokenization is active, enc.encode(text) generates integer token IDs whose count matches the actual context window consumption of OpenAI models. The integer division len(text) // 4 provides an industry-standard approximation for English text and source code when runtime constraints prevent loading the standard tokenizer table.

Parameters: * text (str): The string payload or prompt segment whose tokens are to be counted.

Returns: * int: Total number of tokens computed via BPE encoding or character division approximation.

Raises: * No exceptions are raised directly.

Example: 

# Extracted from log_token_estimation implementation in utils/token_utils.py:
token_count = count_tokens(prompt_content)
percentage = (token_count / max_tokens) * 100 if max_tokens else 0

docs.title: log_token_estimation()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def log_token_estimation(node_name: str, prompt_content: str, max_tokens: int, token_usage: dict | None = None) -> None:

Description: Calculates the token footprint of prompt_content using count_tokens(), determines the percentage against the provided max_tokens context ceiling, and outputs formatted metrics to both stdout and the shared logger. If a breakdown dictionary token_usage is supplied, it calculates the percentage of the total prompt each category occupies and appends it to the log output.

def log_token_estimation(node_name: str, prompt_content: str, max_tokens: int, token_usage: dict | None = None) -> None:
    token_count = count_tokens(prompt_content)
    percentage = (token_count / max_tokens) * 100 if max_tokens else 0

    # Build token usage string if provided
    usage_str = ""
    if token_usage:
        parts = []
        for label, value in token_usage.items():
            pct = (value / token_count * 100) if token_count else 0
            parts.append(f"{label}={value:,} ({pct:.0f}%)")
        usage_str = " | " + " | ".join(parts)

    # Console output (yellow) with token usage
    print(f"\033[93m[Token Analytics] {node_name}: {token_count:,} / {max_tokens:,} tokens ({percentage:.1f}% capacity){usage_str}\033[0m")

    # File log with node context and token usage
    logger.info(f"NODE EXEC | node={node_name} | prompt_tokens={token_count:,} / {max_tokens:,} ({percentage:.1f}% capacity){usage_str}")

log_token_estimation provides real-time observability into the context utilization of each execution node in the knowledge-building pipeline. Terminal output is formatted with ANSI yellow escape codes (\033[93m ... \033[0m) to ensure token budget warnings stand out during execution runs. The structured message is simultaneously logged to logger.info("llm_logger") with prefix NODE EXEC, supporting external parsing and offline token budget auditing. If max_tokens is passed as 0, zero-division is guarded against, assigning percentage = 0.

Parameters: * node_name (str): Identifier of the execution node invoking the token check (e.g., "build_skeleton"). * prompt_content (str): Full prompt text to evaluate. * max_tokens (int): Maximum context window capacity allocated for the node. * token_usage (dict | None, optional): Mapping of sub-component labels to their respective token counts (e.g., {"system_prompt": 120, "context": 4500}). Defaults to None.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions are raised directly.

Example: 

# Core implementation showing console and file log outputs:
token_count = count_tokens(prompt_content)
percentage = (token_count / max_tokens) * 100 if max_tokens else 0

print(f"\033[93m[Token Analytics] {node_name}: {token_count:,} / {max_tokens:,} tokens ({percentage:.1f}% capacity){usage_str}\033[0m")
logger.info(f"NODE EXEC | node={node_name} | prompt_tokens={token_count:,} / {max_tokens:,} ({percentage:.1f}% capacity){usage_str}")
